REUTERS Summary US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that diplomatic efforts with Iran had so far been unproductive because Tehran's demands were unacceptable and unrealistic, speaking to reporters upon arriving in France for a G7 foreign ministers' meeting.
 US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he was “highly unlikely” to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress, CNN reported, citing a phone interview with him.
 A Saudi Aramco administrative building in Riyadh was damaged by falling debris after an attempted attack on Sunday, with no injuries or deaths reported, Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry said.
 The Saudi-led coalition said Sunday that it intercepted and destroyed two Houthi-launched ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, along with two cruise missiles targeting Riyadh and the southern region.
 The UKMTO said on Sunday that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, while another caught fire near Khasab, Oman, prompting its crew to evacuate.
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that mediators had been inactive for several days because of US election results, adding that more time was needed before diplomatic efforts could resume.
 Iran’s Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said on Sunday that a US plan to restrict overland routes for transferring weapons and sanctioned goods would fail. 
 Nov 9, 2026, 00:37 GMT+0 Trump to meet Qatar PM Monday amid Iran mediation efforts
 US President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani on Monday, November 9, the White House said, as Doha continues efforts to mediate between Washington and Tehran.
 Nov 8, 2026, 22:43 GMT+0 Yemen calls on Iran to stop arming Houthis, withdraw IRGC advisers
 Yemen's internationally recognized government called on Iran Sunday to stop arming the Houthis and withdraw its military advisers, accusing Tehran of directly participating in planning and managing the group's operations, according to a statement from Yemen's Foreign Ministry.
 The ministry condemned a statement by Iran's Foreign Ministry concerning Yemen, describing it as interference in Yemen's internal affairs and an attempt to provide political cover for the Houthis.
 It said Yemeni authorities had identified 21 foreign experts working with the Houthis, including 14 members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and seven Hezbollah operatives.
 According to the ministry, their activities include command and control, ballistic missiles, drones, electronic warfare, weapons smuggling and coordinating maritime operations, including selecting commercial vessels for attacks.
 The ministry accused Iran of enabling Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, commercial shipping and navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait.
 It also cited UN Security Council resolutions 2216 and 2624, saying the arms embargo covers weapons, military equipment, technical assistance, training and financing related to military activities.
 The ministry said respecting Yemen's sovereignty required Tehran to stop supplying weapons to the Houthis, withdraw its advisers and end its interference in Yemen's internal affairs.
 Nov 8, 2026, 22:36 GMT+0 Rubio says Iran's demands are 'outrageous and ridiculous,' talks unproductive
 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that diplomatic efforts with Iran had so far been unproductive because Tehran's demands were unacceptable and unrealistic, speaking to reporters upon arriving in France for a G7 foreign ministers' meeting.
 “Right now it hasn't been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic,” Rubio said.
 He said Washington would explore a diplomatic solution if an opportunity emerged, although such efforts were not always possible.
 Rubio also defended President Donald Trump's handling of Iran, saying he had confronted a longstanding threat that previous presidents had failed to address.
 “The president took on something that other presidents have failed to do,” Rubio said, adding that confronting difficult security challenges was sometimes unpopular but necessary.
 Asked about possible US military action, Rubio said American forces would respond defensively to threats against US personnel or commercial shipping in the region.
 “If there's a threat to shipping or to our forces in the region, we have a right to defend ourselves,” he said.
 Nov 8, 2026, 22:11 GMT+0 Trump holds off on Iran strikes as US, Israel prepare for military operation - JPost
 US President Donald Trump held off on ordering renewed military strikes against Iran over the weekend despite preparations by the US and Israeli militaries for a possible operation, The Jerusalem Post reported Sunday, citing two sources.
 Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with top security officials Friday afternoon as Israel prepared for the possibility of a US attack, the report said.
 The US military was also preparing for renewed operations against Iran, but Trump ultimately issued no order to strike.
 Two diplomatic sources told The Jerusalem Post that Trump had given Vice President JD Vance and other senior administration officials “a few days” to reach an agreement with Tehran.
 In an interview with CNN, Trump said renewed military action was “highly unlikely” if negotiations produced a strong agreement.
 “It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump said, adding that he would order strikes if necessary.
 Meanwhile, the US military continued reinforcing its presence in the Middle East, with the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and the amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island reportedly heading toward the region.
 100 % A file photo shows the USS Mason, an Arleigh Burke-class (Flight IIA) Aegis guided-missile destroyer in the United States Navy. Nov 8, 2026, 21:18 GMT+0 Top House Democrat backs Hegseth impeachment, calls for end to Iran war
 US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Sunday he would support a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of engineering what he called a reckless and costly war against Iran, in an interview with ABC News' This Week.
 Jeffries said Democrats would seek to end the Iran war when they take control of Congress in January.
 “We want to do things like end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has made life way too expensive,” he said.
 Asked whether he would support an impeachment resolution against Hegseth that Republican Representative Thomas Massie plans to introduce, Jeffries replied: “I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution.”
 “The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go,” he said.
 Jeffries said House Democrats would discuss the resolution when they reconvene Tuesday, adding that he expected strong support for it.

REUTERS Nov 8, 2026, 21:04 GMT+0 Trump says Iron Gate task force tightening blockade on Iran
 US President Donald Trump said Sunday that Task Force Iron Gate was operating at full strength against Iran, claiming that the US naval blockade had nearly halted the movement of goods into and out of the country.
 "Coupled with history's greatest Naval Blockade, very little gets into, or out of, Iran!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
 Nov 8, 2026, 20:57 GMT+0 Iranian media says US attack caused Qeshm explosions
 The explosions reported earlier on Iran's Qeshm island in the Persian Gulf were caused by a US attack, IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency reported Sunday.
 Tasnim said a projectile fired by US forces had struck the island, adding that Qeshm was the only location where an impact had been reported so far.
 Earlier, state news agency IRNA reported that four explosions had been heard on the island, with several locations apparently struck.
 Nov 8, 2026, 20:48 GMT+0 Khor Mor drone strike knocks 2.8 GW of power generation offline
 Nearly 2,800 megawatts of electricity generation were lost from the grid following Sunday's drone attack on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field, the Kurdistan Region's Electricity Ministry said.
 The disruption followed an explosive-laden drone strike on a gas storage facility at the field in Sulaymaniyah province, sparking a fire.
 Iraq's federal electricity grid was producing about 24,700 megawatts in September, while the Kurdistan Region normally generates around 4,000 to 4,200 megawatts.
 Nov 8, 2026, 20:34 GMT+0 Drone attack sparks fire at Iraqi gas field, production halts reported
 An explosive-laden drone struck a gas storage facility at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field on Sunday, causing a fire and sending thick black smoke into the air.
 An Iraqi security source told Al Hadath that reports had emerged of production being halted at the field, located in Chamchamal in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah province, following the drone attack.
 Nov 8, 2026, 20:19 GMT+0 Iran state media says shots near Sirik part of action against ‘violating vessels’
 Iran’s state broadcaster said three shots heard near Sirik in southern Iran were part of action against what it called “violating vessels” in the Strait of Hormuz.
